definitions.explanation: Bathing in which men and women share the same bath at the same time. Historically common at Japanese hot springs, mixed bathing has become increasingly rare in modern Japan as social norms have changed, but it still exists at some traditional onsen.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{温泉|おんせん}→温泉：04117_onsen⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{混浴|こんよく}だ。
examples.english: This hot spring is mixed bathing.

examples.japanese: {混浴|こんよく}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{露天風呂|ろてんぶろ}→露天風呂：14611_rotenburo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{入|はい}った→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: I went into a mixed-bathing open-air bath.

examples.japanese: ⟦{最近|さいきん}→最近：00881_saikin⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{混浴|こんよく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{廃止|はいし}→廃止：12483_haishi⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧⟦{温泉|おんせん}→温泉：04117_onsen⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{増|ふ}えている→増える：01183_fueru⟧。
examples.english: Recently, more and more hot springs are abolishing mixed bathing.

notes:
USAGE:
{混浴|こんよく} was once the norm at Japanese hot springs, but it has been declining since the Meiji era when Western modesty norms were adopted. Today it survives mainly at remote or traditional onsen in rural areas.

Some mixed baths require bathers to wear a towel or bathing garment. The opposite is ⟦{男女|だんじょ}→男女：03117_danjo⟧⟦{別|べつ}→別：01216_betsu⟧ (gender-separated).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {混浴|こんよく}{風呂|ぶろ}: mixed bath
- {混浴|こんよく}⟦{温泉|おんせん}→温泉：04117_onsen⟧: mixed-bathing hot spring
- {混浴|こんよく}⟦{露天風呂|ろてんぶろ}→露天風呂：14611_rotenburo⟧: mixed-bathing open-air bath
- {混浴|こんよく}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{廃止|はいし}→廃止：12483_haishi⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧: to abolish mixed bathing
